sentence.ja: {電車[でんしゃ]}の中[なか]で食[た]べてはいけません。
sentence.en: You mustn't eat on the train.

mnemonic.story: A *shah* turns his private *den* into a **train** car: velvet sofas, a chandelier that clinks every time the wheels hit a rail joint. Den-sha: train.

sentence.ja: {バス}が来[き]ませんね。
sentence.en: The bus isn't coming, is it?

mnemonic.story: *Bus* is said ba-su, with an open ah instead of uh and a su so light it barely leaves the stop. **Bus**.

sentence.ja: 兄[あに]は新[あたら]しい{車[くるま]}を持[も]っています。
sentence.en: My older brother has a new car.

mnemonic.story: A *cool llama* in sunglasses drives your **car** down the highway, ears flapping out the window. Llama is rama in Japanese, so ku-rama. Kuruma: car.

sentence.ja: あの{自転車[じてんしゃ]}はさくらさんのです。
sentence.en: That bicycle over there is Sakura's.

mnemonic.story: *Gee, ten shahs* wobble past on one **bicycle**, silk robes flapping, the bell ringing. Ji-ten-sha: bicycle.

sentence.ja: 東京[とうきょう]の{地下鉄[ちかてつ]}はとても便利[べんり]です。
sentence.en: The Tokyo subway is really convenient.

mnemonic.story: Under the street the **subway** clatters *chicka-chicka* through the tunnel, iron wheels throwing sparks off iron rails; tetsu means iron. Chika-tetsu: subway.

sentence.ja: 名古屋[なごや]まで{新幹線[しんかんせん]}で行[い]きました。
sentence.en: I went to Nagoya by Shinkansen.

mnemonic.story: The **bullet train** rockets past so close it clips your *shin*, knocks the soda *can* out of your hand and sends a *cent* spinning down the platform. Shin-kan-sen: Shinkansen, bullet train.

sentence.ja: {飛行機[ひこうき]}のチケットを予約[よやく]しました。
sentence.en: I booked a plane ticket.

mnemonic.story: *He* pats his *coat* for the car *key* just as the **airplane** lifts off, and it slips out of the pocket and rattles all the way down the aisle. Hi-kō-ki: airplane.

sentence.ja: 島[しま]まで{船[ふね]}で一時間[いちじかん]かかります。
sentence.en: It takes an hour by boat to the island.

mnemonic.story: A seasick horse stands on the deck of a rocking **ship**, blowing out a long "*foo*" and then a miserable "*neigh*" as the waves slap the hull. Fune: ship, boat.

sentence.ja: {バス停[てい]}で田中[たなか]さんに会[あ]いました。
sentence.en: I ran into Tanaka-san at the bus stop.

mnemonic.story: Basu is the English bus with a vowel on the end; tei means stop. At the **bus stop** the sign just says *stay*, so you stay, rain dripping off the roof. Basu-tei.

sentence.ja: 駅[えき]で{切符[きっぷ]}を買[か]わなければいけません。
sentence.en: I have to buy a ticket at the station.

breakdown.text: 買わなければいけません

mnemonic.story: You feed your **train ticket** into the gate, and a smoked *kipper* slides back out of the slot, warm and fishy, into your hand. Kippu: train ticket.

sentence.ja: {片道[かたみち]}で三時間[さんじかん]かかります。
sentence.en: It takes three hours one way.

mnemonic.story: Michi is road, as in michi o wataru. A giant pizza *cutter* rolls down it and slices away the lane home: **one way** only. Kata-michi: one way.

sentence.ja: 横浜[よこはま]まで{往復[おうふく]}でいくらですか。
sentence.en: How much is a round trip to Yokohama?

mnemonic.story: A big *oaf* of a *cook* rides out to the fish market and straight back, a **round trip**, with a slippery tuna under each arm. Ō-fuku: round trip.

sentence.ja: 新宿[しんじゅく]で{乗[の]り換[か]え}です。
sentence.en: You change trains at Shinjuku.

mnemonic.story: Nori is the stem of noru, to ride, and kae means change: ride, change, a **transfer**. You sprint across the platform yelling "*Car, eh?*" at the next train. Nori-kae: transfer.

sentence.ja: 昨日[きのう]は{終電[しゅうでん]}で帰[かえ]りました。
sentence.en: I went home on the last train yesterday.

mnemonic.story: You sprint for the **last train**, lose a *shoe* on the stairs, and the doors close; you spend the night in a station-side *den*, one sock wet. Shū-den: last train.

sentence.ja: 三番線[さんばんせん]の{ホーム}で待[ま]っています。
sentence.en: I'm waiting on the platform for track three.

mnemonic.story: *Platform* is cut down to its last part, form, which becomes hō-mu. It sounds like home but means a train **platform**.

sentence.ja: {改札[かいさつ]}の前[まえ]で会[あ]いましょう。
sentence.en: Let's meet in front of the ticket gate.

mnemonic.story: A *kite* swoops over the ticket **gate** and drops a *satsuma* onto the card reader, and the flaps snap open for the orange. Kai-satsu: ticket gate.

sentence.ja: 来月[らいげつ]、{旅行[りょこう]}に行[い]きます。
sentence.en: I'm going on a trip next month.

mnemonic.story: You **travel** all the way to *Rio* in a heavy winter *coat*, sweating through the airport while everyone else wears flip-flops. Ryo-kō: travel.

sentence.ja: {世界[せかい]}で一番[いちばん]大[おお]きい国[くに]はどこですか。
sentence.en: What's the biggest country in the world?

mnemonic.story: *Say*, look: your *kite* string runs out so far that the kite circles the whole **world** and bumps you on the back of the head. Se-kai: world.

sentence.ja: 週末[しゅうまつ]に{海[うみ]}へ行[い]きました。
sentence.en: I went to the sea on the weekend.

mnemonic.story: A wave rises out of the **sea** and points a foamy finger at you on the sand. "*Who, me?*" you ask, just before it soaks you in cold salt water. Umi: sea.

sentence.ja: あの{山[やま]}はとても高[たか]いですね。
sentence.en: That mountain is really tall, isn't it?

mnemonic.story: A *llama*, said the Spanish way, yah-mah, stands on top of the **mountain** chewing calmly while you wheeze up the last switchback. Yama: mountain.

sentence.ja: 子供[こども]と{川[かわ]}で遊[あそ]びました。
sentence.en: I played in the river with the kids.

mnemonic.story: Your *car* rolls down the bank into the **river**, and all you can do is wail "*wah!*" as it bobs away on the current. Kawa: river.

sentence.ja: 朝[あさ]の{湖[みずうみ]}はとても静[しず]かです。
sentence.en: The lake is really quiet in the morning.

breakdown.en: of; here 'the lake in the morning'

mnemonic.story: *Mizu*, water, plus *umi*, sea: a sea of water you can drink. You dip a cup in and it tastes sweet, not salty. That's a **lake**. Mizu-umi: lake.

sentence.ja: 山[やま]の{温泉[おんせん]}に泊[と]まりました。
sentence.en: We stayed at a hot spring in the mountains.

mnemonic.story: *On* a dare you flick a *cent* onto the steaming surface of the **hot spring**, and it sinks with a hiss. On-sen: hot spring, spa.

sentence.ja: お寺[てら]で{お土産[みやげ]}を買[か]いました。
sentence.en: I bought souvenirs at the temple.

mnemonic.story: "*Oh, Mia, get* the snow globe!" you shout across the gift shop, and Mia knocks a whole rack of **souvenirs** spinning, glitter swirling in every one. O-miyage: souvenir.

sentence.ja: レストランの{予約[よやく]}は七時[しちじ]です。
sentence.en: The restaurant reservation is at seven.

mnemonic.story: "*Yo, yak!*" the waiter calls, and a shaggy yak lumbers to the best table in the house with a **reservation** card speared on one horn. Yo-yaku: reservation.

sentence.ja: 明日[あした]は{時間[じかん]}がありますか。
sentence.en: Do you have time tomorrow?

mnemonic.story: "*Gee, can* I have more **time**?" you beg as the exam clock ticks over your head. It is the jikan in ichi-jikan, one hour; on its own it means time. Jikan: time.

sentence.ja: 週末[しゅうまつ]、海[うみ]まで{ドライブ}に行[い]きました。
sentence.en: Last weekend we went for a drive to the sea.

mnemonic.story: *Drive* becomes do-ra-i-bu, the v softened to a b. It means a pleasure **drive**, a trip out in the car; the act of driving is unten suru.

sentence.ja: 七時[しちじ]のバスに{乗[の]ります}。
sentence.en: I take the seven o'clock bus.

mnemonic.story: *No rule* says you can't, so you **ride** a camel onto the city bus, its hump brushing the ceiling and its hooves clopping down the aisle. Nor-u: to ride, to board.

sentence.ja: 京都[きょうと]では旅館[りょかん]に{泊[と]まりました}。
sentence.en: In Kyoto we stayed at a ryokan.

mnemonic.story: You **stay** the night in a hotel shaped like a giant *tomato*: the beds are squishy and red, and the whole room smells faintly of ketchup. Toma-ru: to stay (at a hotel).

sentence.ja: うちから学校[がっこう]まで三十分[さんじゅっぷん]{かかります}。
sentence.en: It takes thirty minutes from my house to school.

mnemonic.story: Stuck in traffic, *car*, *car*, *car* as far as you can see, horns honking: the drive **takes** two hours and a whole tank of gas. Kaka-ru: to take (time or money).

sentence.ja: かばんを{持[も]ちましょう}か。
sentence.en: Shall I carry your bag?

mnemonic.story: You **carry** a sandcastle home on a tray, *moats* and all, sea water sloshing over your wrists at every step. Mo-tsu: to carry; to hold.

sentence.ja: 財布[さいふ]を{なくした}んです。
sentence.en: I lost my wallet.

mnemonic.story: You rap your *knuckles* on every pocket, again and again, hollow thud after thud: you've **lost** your keys. Naku-su: to lose.

sentence.ja: ここでバスを{降[お]りて}ください。
sentence.en: Please get off the bus here.

mnemonic.story: An *oriole* hops down the bus steps ahead of you to **get off** at your stop, chirping a thank-you at the driver. Ori-ru: to get off.

sentence.ja: 旅行[りょこう]の日[ひ]を{決[き]めました}。
sentence.en: We decided on the date for the trip.

mnemonic.story: You can't **decide**, so you spin a *key* on the table: if it stops pointing at you, you *may* go. It wobbles, clatters, stops. Kime-ru: to decide.

sentence.ja: 父[ちち]は車[くるま]を{運転[うんてん]する}のが好[す]きです。
sentence.en: My father likes driving.

mnemonic.story: Gripping the wheel on your first lesson, you **drive** at *under ten* kilometres an hour while cyclists ring their bells and pass you. Drop the -der: unten. Unten suru: to drive.

sentence.ja: 来月[らいげつ]、友達[ともだち]とタイを{旅行[りょこう]します}。
sentence.en: Next month I'm traveling around Thailand with a friend.

mnemonic.story: Off to *Rio* in a wool *coat*: you **travel** all the way to the thirty-degree beaches still buttoned up, sweat dripping into your collar. Ryokō suru: to travel.

sentence.ja: 明日[あした]、辞書[じしょ]を{持[も]ってきて}ください。
sentence.en: Please bring a dictionary tomorrow.

mnemonic.story: Motte is mo-tsu, to carry, in its te-form; kuru is to come. Come carrying: **to bring a thing**. You arrive at the picnic carrying the sandcastle, *moats* and all. Motte kuru; for people, tsurete kuru.

sentence.ja: 明日[あした]、妹[いもうと]を{連[つ]れてきます}。
sentence.en: I'll bring my younger sister tomorrow.

mnemonic.story: Tsurete is "taking someone along", kuru is "to come": come with someone, **to bring a person**. You arrive at the party leading *two rays* on leashes, flapping and dripping. Tsurete kuru.

sentence.ja: 明日[あした]は傘[かさ]を{持[も]っていって}ください。
sentence.en: Please take an umbrella tomorrow.

breakdown.text: 持っていってください

mnemonic.story: *Motte*, holding, plus *iku*, go: you **take** a thing by holding it and going, umbrella under your arm as you head out the door. Its twin, motte kuru, holds and comes. Motte iku: to take.

sentence.ja: 駅[えき]まで{どうやって}行[い]きますか。
sentence.en: How do you get to the station?

mnemonic.story: "**How** do we get to the island?" A *doe* on the dock taps her hoof against the side of a *yacht*, clonk, clonk. Dō-yatte: how, by what means.

sentence.ja: 毎日[まいにち]{どのぐらい}勉強[べんきょう]しますか。
sentence.en: How much do you study every day?

mnemonic.story: *Dono* is which and *gurai* is about: about which amount? You keep pouring sugar into your tea, and a friend asks **how much**, then how long you'll keep going. Dono-gurai: how much, how long.

sentence.ja: {どうして}昨日[きのう]クラスに来[き]ませんでしたか。
sentence.en: Why didn't you come to class yesterday?

mnemonic.story: Your bread dough keeps climbing out of the bowl. "*Dough, sh-tay!*" you plead, flour on your nose. **Why** won't it stay? Dōshite: why.

sentence.ja: 犬[いぬ]と猫[ねこ]と{どっち}が好[す]きですか。
sentence.en: Which do you like better, dogs or cats?

mnemonic.story: At the pizza counter: *dough* or *cheese*, **which** do you grab first? Dotchi is the casual way to ask; dochira, the polite one, adds a cheerful ra. Dotchi, dochira: which (of two).

sentence.ja: 毎日[まいにち]{歩[ある]いて}学校[がっこう]へ行[い]きます。
sentence.en: I walk to school every day.

mnemonic.story: "*Are we* there yet?" your little brother whines, three hours **on foot** up a dusty trail, sandals flapping. Arui-te: on foot, walking.

sentence.ja: 去年[きょねん]、{初[はじ]めて}日本[にほん]へ行[い]きました。
sentence.en: Last year I went to Japan for the first time.

mnemonic.story: It starts like *hajimemashite*, the hello for someone new. You bow to a snowman you are meeting **for the first time** and shake its cold twig hand. Hajimete.

sentence.ja: {ゆっくり}食[た]べてください。
sentence.en: Please eat slowly.

mnemonic.story: *You, coolly*, rock on a porch swing and sip iced tea **slowly**, ice cubes clinking, while everyone else rushes past. Yukkuri: slowly, at your leisure.

sentence.ja: 毎日[まいにち]二時間[にじかん]{ぐらい}勉強[べんきょう]します。
sentence.en: I study for about two hours every day.

mnemonic.story: Grandma never measures: she slaps **about** two fistfuls of *gooey rye* dough into the bowl, roughly right every time. Gurai: about, after a number or amount.
